pages.hook: In New York City, you can buy pizza by the slice and eat it on the street in two minutes. Learn how to order, pay and eat it like a New Yorker.
pages.polite: Say **Can I get…?** or **Two slices, please**, then **Thanks!** Keep it short; the line is moving.

mythfact.s: In New York, many pizza shops sell single slices.
mythfact.why: You can order one, two or more slices and eat right away.

mythfact.s: People often fold a New York slice before they eat it.
mythfact.why: The slice is large and thin, so folding it is easy and clean.

mythfact.s: Pepperoni is a very common topping in the USA.
mythfact.why: Pepperoni is one of the most popular pizza toppings in the USA.

mythfact.s: You must use a knife and a fork to eat a slice.
mythfact.why: Most people eat a slice with their hands.

mythfact.s: A “soda” in the USA is a type of cake.
mythfact.why: A soda is a fizzy soft drink.

decode.q: How much are one pepperoni slice and a large soda?

lines: Please do not sit without ordering

compare.br: In Brazil, pizza is often a whole pie shared by a group, at a pizzeria or delivery, with a knife and fork or by hand.
compare.us: In New York, a quick slice is a street meal: you stand, eat with your hands and pay a few dollars.
compare.tip: Know your numbers: three dollars is “three dollars”, not “three”.
compare.ask: How do you eat pizza? With your hands or knife and fork? Say it in English.

The price is eight dollars. You give the money and say…

pages.title: Cultural spotlight · Quiz
Reading quest — My first slice in New York · part 1
text: Today I am in **New York**, and I am very hungry. On the corner, I see a pizza shop with a big sign: “Pizza by the slice.” I go in.

A man called Ravi says, “Hi! **What can I get you?**” I say, “**Two slices of pepperoni, please.**” He puts the slices in a hot oven, and in a minute they are ready. “**Anything to drink?**” he asks. “A soda, please.” “**Small or large?**” “Large. **How much is it?**” “**That’s eight dollars.**” I say, “**Here you go. Thanks!**” and he says, “**Enjoy your pizza!**”
The slices are huge! A woman next to me **folds** her slice in half and eats it with her hands. I do the same. It is hot, cheesy and so good. A man says, “**New York style, baby!**”

opts: Buying pizza by the slice in New York
fast.why: The writer buys pizza slices in New York.

How much is it?
What does the woman do with her slice?

tf.s: The pizza shop sells whole pizzas only.
tf.why: The sign says “Pizza by the slice.”

tf.s: The writer orders a large soda.
tf.why: “Large. How much is it?”

tf.s: The writer pays nine dollars.
tf.why: The price is eight dollars; the writer gives ten.

tf.s: The writer eats with hands.
tf.why: The writer folds the slice and eats it.

pages.title: Reading quest — My first slice in New York · part 2
text: I remember a song from my English class, “This Old Man”. It is a British counting song, written down in the early 1900s. It counts from one to ten, and each number has a rhyme. I count my dollars too: one, two, three… up to ten.
I give Ravi ten dollars, and he gives me two dollars back. “**Keep the change**,” I say, and I smile. It is a great lunch, and it costs only a few dollars.
